sourceFindings.finding: Permit is unique by case_id, attempt_id and identity, with primary key(scope_id,case_id). valid_until must be after admitted_at and at most60 minutes after admitted_at. A second row for this same case/attempt is rejected.
All v2 tables, explicitly including permits, have immutable BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE and no_reset BEFORE TRUNCATE triggers. Copying the old record elsewhere would not authorise rewriting it.
Only scope-and-first-case and next-case modes exist. The bounded deadline is validated and one new permit is INSERTed. There is no renewal, replacement or conflict-update mode.

The RPC selects that one stored permit, preserves full identity and original-history/cap guards, and denies expired scope or permit. inspect and begin_case remain denied; submit_slot cannot dispatch after expiry.

Late receipt_slot/finish_case support bookkeeping for actual submitted/claimed work. They do not issue a new permit, reserve an unused case, fabricate mandatory receipts or start an expired unclaimed case.
The operator sequence requires an independently inspected immutable named-run permit. Expiry can permit evidence recording but blocks new submissions; no unused-permit renewal procedure is supplied.

Owner funding/scope approval remains bounded at24 hours, zero retries and the fixed reviewed runtime/plan. It separately states each named run permit expires within60 minutes and contains no approved renewal mechanism.

conclusion: There is no supported execution continuation using the current expired permit under the existing accepted schema/builder/RPC. A still-current overall approval does not itself renew the per-run deadline. Keep the job unreleased and runner NOLOGIN.
forbiddenWorkarounds: In-place deadline or admitted_at update, including after copying the original row elsewhere.

Re-inserting the same case under a new run or attempt, treating late-bookkeeping RPCs as dispatch authority, or fabricating completion/absence/accounting.
